observationsNotFindings: The corpus-phrase citation is the detail worth recording, because the obvious check fails and the artifact is still right. G26 v1 has no namedCorpusNotAuthored key at all, unlike the G24 harness, so a reviewer comparing that field finds null. The subject never claims otherwise: it cites liveHarnessCellVerbatim, the field that does carry the phrase, and its own namedCorpusNotAuthored is a local structure rather than a claim about the harness's schema. The phrase is an exact suffix of that field, which is itself byte-identical to the live register cell.

Two obligations exist purely to hold standings that this gate is unusually positioned to erode, and both cite live sources I confirmed. OBL-G17-REMAINS-INAPPLICABLE matters most: G26 is the SARIF-not-advertised gate, so it sits closer than any other artifact to the dropped SARIF-parity harness, and a join that drifted would restore G17 by implication rather than by statement. Recording the standing as its own obligation makes the non-restoration checkable instead of assumed.

As with the G24 join, the recording's own historical cardinalities are left behind - D-152 records required-now becoming twenty-two with twenty-three OPEN, and none of those numbers appears here against a live 26. Three joins in this sweep have now shown that discipline independently, which suggests it is a convention rather than luck.

OBL-G26-FX-AUTHORING is the single open obligation and, as with G24, its corpus is one phrase rather than an enumerated class list. A later fixture cycle inherits a phrase and a one-class scope. G26 is narrower still than G24, since it owns NT-5 alone.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. The land test passes on the register: the live file 08 DR-G26 status cell reads OPEN and that is what the subject carries, with registerRowNote stating why DR-G26's own token belongs in that field rather than DR-131's standing. The check worth recording is the corpus phrase, because the obvious comparison fails and the artifact is still correct. The subject never claims it has one: it cites liveHarnessCellVerbatim, the field that does carry the phrase, and the phrase is an exact suffix of that field, which is itself byte-identical to the live register harness cell. Its own namedCorpusNotAuthored is a local structure, not a claim about the harness schema. Scope is tight - NT-5 occurs seventeen times and every other NT identifier occurs zero times - and matches live D-152, which records that G26 owns DR-131 NT-5 only and that NT-5 leftover-design closes with the remainder being G26 execution. G17 is the standing this particular gate is most positioned to erode, and the artifact holds it with a dedicated obligation citing D-077 and G26 v1's EV-2 passProperty, both of which check out, with the live register evidence cell saying the same. D-152's historical cardinalities of twenty-two and twenty-three are not imported against a live 26.
